questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to take the opportunity of going outside if Europe, since studying is a relatively easy way of going somewhere without having to apply for jobs, long term visas etc. I love the ocean and warm weather and Cape Town didn't only have that, but also nature, city, culture (and wine). I speak several languages from before but this time I wanted to focus on experiencing the place and getting to know people, therefore I chose an English-speaking country. I didn't know much about University of Cape Town but when I listened to the principal's beginning of semester speech online while still being in Denmark, I felt it was something different than I was used to in the Nordics. There's another level of authenticity and humanity highly influenced by the very recent history of apartheid.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was going to take courses within the anthropology department but ended up not actually being able to take any of them because they were cancelled last minute. Now I'm very happy about that because instead I got to connect with people from different departments and fields. My courses were in medicine&art, gender development and conflict in SA, and linguistics.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The studies were half in person and half online so it was quite messy. Mainly to manage to register to courses and understanding the system since no one answered any emails. In the end a "deadline for enrollment" wasn't as set in stone as I thought and I could have avoided stressing about it if I knew that.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: To be honest not much. The international team did organize some online sessions but to get answers to your questions was quite difficult.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through a friend that had been in Cape Town the year before.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to get to know  people from other settings in SA it is definitely worth living off campus. I didn't intend to "spend my life" on campus so for me it was a great choice. Most SA students are also very young in my experience as they go studying right away after school, which made me older than most (27 as postgraduate)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Can't really say.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We did it online. But to be registered for courses you need to have signatures from course convenors and then submit that form to apply to the course in the student portal online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: IAPO. But as mentioned it wasn't easy to get answers.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted that were offered but many were cancelled last minute or only offered during the second semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't panic! Things will work out, many are in the same situation as you :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved my courses actually but as they were not in my field it was a bit demanding. A lot of work, more than I've ever had to do before.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A lot of written reports, and quite long ones. The courses had completely different requirements though.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers and students were much closer in Cape Town. They were more personal and met their students at eye level. People were also sharing about profound suffering in their lives in class, and the teacher met it with kindness.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't participate in anything so can't say.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. Everything from scuba diving and hiking, to volunteering.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Volunteering! Just to move out of the campus bubble, to see other sides of Cape Town and understand the socio-economic situation in society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Wine tastings, beaches, road trips, eating out, yogs etc etc

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Surprisingly easy. I felt very at home, probably because it's so western-like.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in your classes. Ask questions when not understanding something instead of just assuming

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That I felt I came from a very privileged context and didn't always feel entitled to express my opinion or view in certain situations. Not because they said so but because I thought it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The incredible kindness. People are insanely kind.  You will notice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) In Cape Town you really get everything, ocean, mountain, nature, beach,city - use it and don't bury yourself in studies and books.
2) No matter how used or not used you are to travel there's always a level of loneliness in the beginning. Embrace that it will pass, engage in activities around you.
3) if you care a lot about grades you should know it's difficult to get good grades from UCT. They have a scale going to 100% but no one receives more than maximum around 80. When the grades then are transferred back to UCPH it might not look as good as you want them to.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't have to pay administration fees (you pay nothing) to UCT. This was unclear to me, I payed and fortunately I should get it refunded.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The environment, the people, the history.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Quite a lot of administrative struggles that took a lot of energy. If you live far from campus that can be a struggle to go there a lot but since I was doing combined online and in person teaching it was fine (lived in Sea point and studied at Upper Campus).

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
